change_description: EXISTING BUG (reframed 2026-05-14 -- see notes): LEAGUE_FIRST_INNING_RUNS = 0.475 hardcoded in mlb_first_inning_predictor.py line 74 is ~7% understated vs 2024+2025 empirical mean of 0.510 runs per first half-inning (4802 game-half-innings sampled from data/backtests/backtest_2024-*_truepit.csv and backtest_2025-*_truepit.csv). The constant is tagged '2023-2024 seasons' verified 2026-01-15 -- effectively a pre-pitch-clock estimate that did not get refreshed when 2025 offense pushed up. CORRECTED ANALYSIS: this is NOT a quick fix and the original framing 'likely cause of suppressed STRONG YRFI rate, isolate after Phase 2.1' set up a false expectation. The constant is the base anchor at predictor.py:845 (lam = LEAGUE_FIRST_INNING_RUNS * o_mult * p_mult * pf * home_fact) so all lambdas in the system are scaled ~7% low -- but three downstream consumers compensate end-to-end: (1) calibration_v2.json was fit against actual outcomes using these understated raw probs, so calibrated nrfi_prob is correct end-to-end; (2) the 0.78 LAMBDA_YRFI_FLOOR was empirically tuned ON the understated lambdas (comment at predictor.py:945 documents '0.74-0.78 bucket went 4W-5L, filtering lifts +1.36u'), so the gate is internally consistent in stale-units and is correctly kicking out a real money-losing bucket; (3) only diagnostic surfaces (model-expected-runs chip on dashboard, lambda values in pick_reasoning_log) are cosmetically biased low. Live bet selection currently correct. Fixing requires the full recalibration cascade: update constant -> re-derive LAMBDA_YRFI_FLOOR (mechanically 0.838, or refit empirically) -> refit calibration_v2.json on the new raw distribution -> 3-split OOS validation -> 7-day shadow window. Touches 5+ files: predictor.py, recalibrate_v2.py, calibration_v2.json, plus 4 mirror-constants in tools/v23_walkforward_backtest.py + tools/v21_shadow_predict.py + tools/backtest_v2_truepit_2026.py + scripts/archive/regrade_and_rebet.py. DO NOT swap in isolation -- a naive constant update shifts the raw distribution out from under the calibrator that was fit against it, introducing inconsistency rather than fixing it. Filed for a future model-refresh project alongside park-factor rebuild + calibrator refit + i01 sitCode fix (row 2026-05-12-bug-prior-season-pitcher-fi-i1). Explicitly out of scope for Phase 4 operational hardening per 2026-05-14 triage decision.
notes: Discovered 2026-05-12 during Phase 2.1 Q3 empirical FI ERA verification. Year-by-year: 2024 = 0.489 runs/half (4.40 FI 'ERA' on total runs, ~4.22 earned-only), 2025 = 0.532 runs/half (4.79 / ~4.60). The 0.475 constant appears to be a pre-pitch-clock (pre-2023) estimate that did not get refreshed when pitch clock pushed offense up. Year-over-year delta of +0.39 ERA between 2024 and 2025 is itself a separate finding -- see Phase 2.1 month-by-month diagnostic on the same date. REFRAMED 2026-05-14 during Phase 4 kickoff triage: original gate_result=BUG_FILED implied a fix-it-when-convenient bug; the calibration-cascade analysis above shows it is instead a model-refresh project. Promoted to DEFERRED and explicitly out of Phase 4 scope. The correction to this row is itself the deliverable of the 2026-05-14 triage -- the original framing risked someone naively swapping the constant later and breaking the calibrator. Future model-refresh project should bundle this with the i01 sitCode fix (real first-inning ERA data being silently zeroed) and the park-factor rebuild, all touching the same recalibrate_v2.py code path.

change_description: Phase 2.2 -- pitcher first-pitch strike % in 1st inning.  Bayesian-blended FPS_1st per pitcher, shrunk to single league prior LEAGUE_FPS_1ST_AVG=0.62 (empirically 0.6194 across 92547 events 2021-2026) with N_PRIOR_FPS=20 events.  Adds home_first_pitch_strike_pct to T1 and away_first_pitch_strike_pct to B1 (19 features per half total vs phase-e3's 18).  Per-pitch Statcast pull via pybaseball; year-stable post-pitch-clock environment so no year-indexing needed (unlike Phase 2.1 FIE). gate_result: FAIL -- 2/3 splits favored candidate (gate 1 PASS) but S3 delta -0.0001 vs threshold -0.003 (gate 2 FAIL, 30x below).  Distinct from FIE's pattern: FIE had 1/3 wins (S1/S2 exactly 0.0000); FPS has 2/3 wins (real-signed negative deltas on S2+S3).  Filed as FAIL per playbook (the threshold is the threshold) but mechanistically different.
notes: Feature has real signal -- 2-of-3 splits favored candidate -- but signal magnitude is too small to clear the -0.003 S3 gate.  Coefficient magnitudes (T1=-0.0190, B1=-0.0173, both signed correctly negative since higher FPS -> fewer runs allowed) survive the existing 18-feature stack and produce the most symmetric pitcher-quality feature in the model (T1/B1 ratio 1.10x, vs FIP 12x, xERA 16x, FIE 2x).  Marginal Brier contribution is ~0.0001, not 0.003.  Pre-Gate-A diagnostics ALL pointed at a real feature (Q5 mean |delta| 4.3pp, stddev 5.2pp; named-pitcher archetypes mapping correctly; deGrom topping the league at 0.7121; Brady Basso bottoming at 0.4391).  The trained model IS using FPS -- it's just not enough to move the meta-aggregate Brier by 30bp.  Mild whiff_pct_rank absorption (~7-8% shift more negative) suggests FPS captures something correlated-but-not-identical to whiff-based count leverage.  Per playbook 'Common Pitfalls #2', FPS is shelved without iteration.  No L2 sweep, no prior adjustment, no current-season-to-date refinement.  This row is distinct from FIE: if a future feature interacts favorably with FPS (e.g. a count-leverage feature that's orthogonal to whiff and FPS both), this is the row to revisit.  More broadly, this is information about how close to optimal V2.2 already is on the existing data sources -- a feature that 'should' help based on Q5-style pre-diagnostics, trains with meaningful coefficients, passes named-pitcher smell tests, can still fail to clear a 0.003 Brier gate.  Trained weights left at data/candidates/v23_fps/ for reproducibility.  Phase 2.2 closed 2026-05-14.  Next: Phase 2.3 leadoff hitter isolation (per playbook ordering).

notes: Gate A failed both criteria. All three splits returned TIE (deltas within +/-0.0001).  Mechanistically the pre-Gate-A weight inspection foretold this: trained FIE coefficients were tiny (T1=+0.0069, B1=+0.0035, signed correctly) vs xera ~0.04 and top3c_iso ~0.4.  The FIE T1/B1 asymmetry was ~2x, MILDER than FIP (~12x) or xERA (~16x), indicating FIE carries comparatively uniform signal across halves -- but that uniform signal is small in absolute terms. Per playbook 'Common Pitfalls #2 -- p-hacking the feature definition', FIE is shelved without iteration.  No L2 sweep, no lookback adjustment, no current-season-to-date V1.1 attempt -- if the V1 feature design produces zero marginal Brier signal across 3 splits with sample N=4802, the answer is not 'try a different definition' but 'this feature is captured by existing signals'. Drops to +2.53pp in 2025 (n=220, model 65.71% vs actual 63.18%) and +0.51pp in 2026 (n=11, model 64.14% vs actual 63.64%).  This is historical environment drift (pitch-clock era), not active leak. notes: Identified 2026-05-14 during Phase 2.3 vs Phase 3.2 read-only pivot investigation. change_description: Phase 2.3 backfill uses fetch_top3_batters which prefers post-game boxscore.battingOrder (actual lineup) and falls back to schedule.lineups (announced lineup).  Production at predict-time hits schedule.lineups first (boxscore empty pre-pitch).  ~5% of slots differ across the two sources due to late scratches.  NOT a stat-level leak -- both sources get strict-less-than date stat cutoffs at backtest.py:1501 (relevant = [g for g in log if g['date'] < target_date_iso]).  Estimated training-signal effect ~0.1pp from 0.05 * 7pp * 1/3, inside noise of natural OBP variance.  Accepted deliberately: training on actual batting order correctly attributes 1st-inning labels to the batters who created them; predict-time announced lineup is the best available estimate.  Documented for institutional memory.
notes: Identified 2026-05-14 during Phase 2.3 pre-backfill leakage review.  The hard-gate leakage check (per-batter stat cutoff) PASSED -- this finding is the separate, smaller composition asymmetry that surfaced while reading the source.  Alternative would be reordering fetch_top3_batters to query schedule.lineups first, but the MLB Stats API likely doesn't retain historical announced lineups for closed seasons, so strict prod-time semantics may not be achievable for backfill anyway.  Train/serve consistency framing: the backfill teaches the model 'this batter at this prior-stat level correlates with NRFI', and production at predict-time provides the announced-batter's prior stats as the best available proxy.  Both sides see prior-only data.  If a future analysis asks 'why does V2.3 train Brier look slightly better than walk-forward Brier?', this asymmetry is a candidate explanation worth examining.

change_description: BUG: tools/candidate_validation.py --fps help text contains a bare '%' (the string 'first-pitch strike % in 1st inning') that crashes argparse's --help formatter with TypeError ('%i format: a real number is required, not dict').  argparse's _expand_help applies %-substitution to help strings using a params dict; the bare '%' followed by ' in' is interpreted as a partial format spec.  Introduced 2026-05-14 when Phase 2.2 --fps flag was added.  COSMETIC ONLY -- does not affect non-help invocations.  argparse builds the parser at module import time; _format_help / _expand_help only run when --help is invoked.  Verified by running 'python tools/candidate_validation.py --phase-e3 --fps --candidate /tmp/x' which built the parser and proceeded normally into a Gate A pass.  One-character fix: '%' -> '%%' in the help string (argparse strips the escape during expansion).  Defer -- not blocking Phase 2.3.
notes: Same isolation rule as other deferred bugs: fix in own commit after Phase 2.3 closes.  Note that two_stage_model.py uses '%%' correctly in its own --clean-only help (line 527: '~22%% of historical'), so the pattern is already known in the codebase -- this was just an oversight when Phase 2.2 was added to the validator.

T1/B1 each 18->19 features (net +1 per half, +2 params total). gate_result: FAIL -- 0/3 splits favored candidate (gate 1 FAIL, worse than FIE 1/3 and FPS 2/3), S3 delta +0.0003 vs threshold -0.003 (gate 2 FAIL, wrong direction).  Gate C elite-power S3 delta +0.0042 PASSED only because +0.005 threshold was deliberately loose for n=71; candidate is worse on elite-power too, no silver lining there.
notes: STRUCTURAL FAILURE, NOT TUNING PROBLEM.  Weight inspection on the trained candidate (before Gate A ran) diagnosed the mechanism: a linear LR cannot exploit within-lineup anti-correlation via a level-split.  The Q5 finding (r = -0.27 negative correlation between leadoff_obp and 2_3_combined_obp within a lineup) is real but is a property of CROSS-LINEUP VALUE VARIATION -- it doesn't translate to opposite-signed LR coefficients because both features still contribute positively to 'offense scores in 1st.'  All four new coefficients trained POSITIVE: T1 leadoff +0.0501, T1 2_3 +0.0539, B1 leadoff +0.0020, B1 2_3 +0.0860.  T1 baseline aggregate was +0.1726; split sum 0.1040 LOST ~40% of signal as L2 shrank both correlated-team-quality halves.  B1 baseline aggregate +0.0512; split sum 0.0880 with all signal concentrated in 2_3 (leadoff near zero).  Asymmetry (T1 vs B1 leadoff coefficient ratio 25x) likely L2-amplified noise on small signals.  Per playbook 'Common Pitfalls #2 -- p-hacking the feature definition', LEADOFF is shelved without iteration.  No L2 sweep, no prior adjustment, no AB-floor variant, no alternative weighting scheme -- the architecture limitation (linear level-split cannot capture the shape signal we want) means tweaking the definition would only re-fail more elaborately.  Three Phase 2.x features in a row have now failed Gate A on similar grounds (FIE: features redundant with FIP/xERA/last5/last10/pvt; FPS: real signal but too small; LEADOFF: real cross-lineup signal but inexpressible in linear-level-split form).  Cumulative evidence that V2.2 is at its plateau on existing data sources under the linear-level architecture.  See companion audit row 2026-05-14-finding-phase3-interaction-architecture for the architecturally-correct way to exploit the LEADOFF anti-correlation finding -- a Phase 3 idea, NOT a Phase 2.4 quick-add.  Trained weights left at data/candidates/v23_leadoff/ for reproducibility.  Phase 2.3 closed 2026-05-14.

change_description: Phase 2.3 LEADOFF (Gate A FAIL 0/3) revealed a methodological limitation: a linear level-split feature cannot exploit within-lineup anti-correlation.  The architecturally-correct way to capture the Q5 finding (r = -0.27 leadoff_obp vs 2_3_combined_obp within lineups) is an INTERACTION FEATURE -- candidate forms include: (1) `lineup_spread` = |leadoff_obp - 2_3_combined_obp| as a separate feature; (2) `lineup_product` = leadoff_obp * 2_3_combined_obp; (3) a non-linear stage on top of the existing LR (gradient boost on residuals, or a tiny MLP).  All three would let the model express 'the SHAPE of the lineup matters, not just the levels' -- which is exactly what the anti-correlation finding implies should help.  Filed as a FINDING for institutional memory.
notes: This is a Phase 3 architecture idea, NOT a Phase 2.4 quick-add.  Reasoning: Phase 2 has been level-feature additions/splits within the existing LR architecture -- compatible with the production loader, recalibrate_v2.py, the shadow gate, etc.  Adding an interaction term or non-linear stage would require: (a) deciding which interaction (the three candidate forms above all involve different data assumptions), (b) updating production loader to accept the new feature, (c) updating recalibrate_v2.py to fit the larger model, (d) deciding whether the calibrator architecture still applies cleanly downstream of a non-linearity.  These are coordinated changes, not a one-feature-add.  Recording the idea so it's preserved for the next strategic conversation.  If the operator decides to pivot to Phase 3, the LEADOFF data (already backfilled across 2024+2025+2026) is the natural test ground -- the existing lineup_json columns make the interaction features cheap to compute.  Do NOT pivot to this as a reflex after Phase 2.3 FAIL; treat as deliberate strategic decision.

change_description: Sign-flip falsification methodology established 2026-05-16.  When the operator suspects the model is 'backwards' (e.g. 'NRFI bets are going YRFI and vice versa'), the decisive test is the full predictive surface, not bet outcomes.  Pull all graded games (NOT just STRONG bet_placed=Y, since bet selection biases the sample toward p_nrfi in [0.6, 0.7]).  Bin by predicted nrfi_prob in 5-10pp wide buckets and compute Spearman rank correlation between predicted P(NRFI) and observed 1/0 NRFI outcomes.  Decision rule: rho approx -0.5 or worse = sign-flip; rho approx 0 = signal loss; rho > 0 = healthy.  Secondary check: the highest-NRFI-pred bin (0.60-0.70) hit rate -- under sign-flip this bin should hit NRFI < 40%; under normal operation it hits ~65%.  95% CI on rho via Fisher transform: lo = tanh(atanh(rho) - 1.96/sqrt(n-3)), hi = tanh(atanh(rho) + 1.96/sqrt(n-3)).  Typical recent-window sample sizes: 3d n~40, 7d n~80, 14d n~170, 30d n~390, season n~600.
notes: Established during the 2026-05-16 sign-flip investigation triggered by operator perception 'NRFI games going YRFI and vice versa' after the 5/13-5/15 STRONG-Y stretch (7W-5L, -0.308u realized, z=-0.18 vs expected variance band).  Investigation result: Spearman rho across windows fell in [-0.055, +0.075]; 95% CIs all included zero AND small positive values -- quantitatively incompatible with sign-flip (which would require rho approx -0.5 over n>=77).  Secondary check passed too: highest-NRFI-pred bin (0.60-0.70) hit 57% over 7d / 68% season-long, fully calibrated.  Verdict: NORMAL OPERATION.  Methodology saved here so the next 'is the model backwards' check reruns the exact procedure without reinventing the test.  Future implementation candidate: tools/sign_flip_check.py accepting --window {3d,7d,14d,30d,season}.  Data source data/picks_2026.csv columns actual_result + nrfi_prob; filter actual_result in (NRFI, YRFI) AND nrfi_prob is not blank.  Companion finding 2026-05-16-finding-season-rho-baseline records the current baseline rho the procedure should be measured against.

change_description: Architecture Path 1 (XGBoost on LR + isotonic calibrator residuals) tested with two framings, both FAIL Gate A.  Framing A (regression on residuals, conservative hyperparams max_depth=2, eta=0.02, 40 rounds, reg_lambda=10): wins 1/3 splits; S1 +0.0025, S2 +0.0012, S3 -0.0009 -- below the -0.003 threshold.  Framing B (binary classifier with LR_cal_prediction appended as feature, max_depth=3, eta=0.03, 80 rounds): wins 0/3; S1 +0.0050, S2 +0.0017, S3 +0.0032.  Default-hyperparam residual regression overfit by 1-1.5pp Brier on every split.  Implication: the LR + isotonic calibrator is at its information ceiling for the current 18-feature space.  Boost cannot extract more non-linear signal because the signal isn't there to extract.  The next architectural lever is NOT more model capacity -- it is new data sources (Path 3 in the 2026-05-19 session sketch): batter splits vs starter handedness (column exists but unused), catcher framing (tools exist, not in LR), days rest, wind direction, pitch arsenal recency.
notes: Established during 2026-05-19 session, after the model-refresh ship.  Tool: tools/train_boost_residual.py (not committed -- experiment-only). change_description: Engineered DIFF variant of the vs-handedness feature also FAILs Gate A and actually performs WORSE than the raw VSHAND.  Feature definition: top3_vs_oppHand_diff = top3_ops_vs_oppHand - (top3c_obp + top3c_slg), designed to isolate the incremental platoon signal by subtracting the season-OPS baseline.  Hypothesis was that the raw VSHAND failure was multicollinearity with top3c_obp/slg -- a DIFF feature is mathematically orthogonal to those baselines.  Results: S1 baseline 0.2511 -> candidate 0.2514, delta +0.0003 (wrong direction).  S2 baseline 0.2595 -> candidate 0.2599, delta +0.0004 (wrong direction).  Both worse than baseline.  Trained weights still POSITIVE on T1 (+0.0542 to +0.1346) -- the orthogonal-by-construction DIFF feature STILL gets a wrong-sign weight, which means the noise in the per-game DIFF estimate is correlated with NRFI outcomes by chance, not signal.  Compared to raw VSHAND (-0.0002 both splits), engineering HURT performance by an additional 0.0005-0.0006 -- the DIFF amplifies the per-game noise without adding signal.  Conclusion: vs-handedness OPS for top-3 batters carries no usable predictive signal for first-inning NRFI in this dataset, regardless of framing.
